item.title: Wed 11 Nov 06:35 · risk-off · Zcash briefly breaks below $1,000 as bitcoin clings to $73,000
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Zcash fell about 12% on Tuesday and briefly traded below $1,000 for the first time since early September, as Grayscale trust redemptions added selling.
  2. Bitcoin's low on Tuesday was deeper than first reported, about $72,640 on Coinbase, but it closed the day near $73,800, above the $73,000 line analysts were watching.
  3. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.00% after the hot inflation report, and the Nasdaq fell 0.7% with Nvidia down 5.5%.

What changed: Last night's question was whether bitcoin's daily close would hold $73,000. It did, so the line held for now. The new damage is in Zcash, which lost more than bitcoin on the same macro shock. Next to watch: US PPI on Friday 13 November at 13:30 UK. The next big event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Zcash briefly breaks below $1,000 as bitcoin clings to $73,000

Zcash fell about 12% in a day, its sharpest drop in weeks, while bitcoin dipped to a near three-month low before closing just above a level traders had marked as critical.

Zcash fell as low as $999.57 on Tuesday, its weakest level since early September, Seeking Alpha and Bitcoin.com News reported. The token was down about 12% over 24 hours and roughly 41% below its 2026 high of $1,695, reached on 26 September.

Seeking Alpha linked the fall to leveraged long positions being forced shut and to continuing redemptions from the Grayscale Zcash Trust, which require the trust to sell or withdraw the coins it holds. The same day, Grayscale launched a $1 million Zcash ecosystem programme, with $400,000 in first grants.

Bitcoin also hit its lowest level since late August. Coinbase data showed a low of $72,643 at 16:38 UTC on Tuesday, Forbes reported, after October's US inflation figures came in hotter than forecast. It recovered to about $73,800 by midnight UTC, according to KuCoin market data.

The pressure came from bond markets as well. The US 10-year Treasury yield rose about 14 basis points to 5.00%, TheStreet reported, and the Nasdaq fell 0.74%. Fed Vice Chair Michelle Bowman said in a speech that inflation progress had stalled and that policy was "not on a preset course".

Selling by large holders added to the mood. Bitcoin miner MARA said it had sold 13,597 bitcoin, about $1.1 billion, since 30 September and planned to sell more, CoinDesk reported.

Traders now look to US producer prices on Friday and the Fed's decision on 9 December.

Zcash fell about 12% and briefly broke $1,000, while bitcoin dipped to about $72,640 before closing near $73,800. US 10-year yields hit 5% and the miner MARA said it has sold $1.1 billion of bitcoin since September.

  1. 🔴 Outlook changed Zcash Desk: Zcash falls about 12% and briefly trades below $1,000 (High confidence). ZEC hit $999.57, its lowest since early September and about 41% below its 26 September high of $1,695. On Monday it was near $1,165, so the fall has sped up. Seeking Alpha cites forced selling of leveraged longs and Grayscale Zcash Trust redemptions, which add spot selling. Seeking Alpha Bitcoin.com News Analytics Insight
  2. 🔴 Developing Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin's low was about $72,640, but the daily close held above $73,000 (High confidence). Coinbase showed a low of $72,643 at 16:38 UTC on Tuesday, the weakest since about 21 August. Bitcoin then closed the UTC day near $73,800, so the $73,000 close analysts flagged held. They name $70,000 as the next level below and $74,500 to $75,000 as the zone to reclaim. Forbes KuCoin daily market report CoinDesk
  3. 🟠 Developing Markets: US 10-year yield closes at 5.00%; Nasdaq falls 0.7% as Nvidia drops 5.5% (High confidence). The 10-year yield rose about 14 basis points on the inflation report and the 2-year about 18 basis points to 4.73%. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Nasdaq 0.74%. A 5% risk-free yield makes non-yielding assets like bitcoin less attractive to hold. US bond markets are closed today for Veterans Day. TheStreet StockTitan
  4. 🟠 New Bitcoin Desk: Miner MARA has sold 13,597 bitcoin since September and plans to sell more (High confidence). MARA said with its third-quarter results that it sold about $1.1 billion of bitcoin after 30 September, repaid $750m of bitcoin-backed loans, and will keep selling to fund AI infrastructure, debt and possible buybacks. It held 34,012 BTC at 30 September. Steady selling from a large holder adds supply while ETF demand is weak. CoinDesk Cryptonews.net (citing MARA's shareholder letter)
  5. 🟠 Developing ETFs and Institutions: ETF outflows slow to about $95m on Tuesday; IBIT redemptions continue (Medium confidence). Early figures show a net outflow of about $95m, with IBIT down $78m, Fidelity's FBTC down $37m and Morgan Stanley's MSBT up $20m. That is smaller than Monday's $201m, but it would be IBIT's eighth straight day of redemptions. Outflows since 2 November are about $1.5bn. KuCoin (TechFlow) TFTC ETF tracker
  6. 🟠 New The Big Picture: Fed's Bowman: inflation progress has stalled, policy 'not on a preset course' (High confidence). Vice Chair Bowman said core PCE inflation likely rose to 3.3% in October and there is "still work to do", but stopped short of backing a hike and said tightening must be weighed against costs such as housing. She is often among the more dovish officials, so a hawkish tone from her narrows the case for a pause. Federal Reserve
  7. 🟢 New Protocol and Development: Zcash NU8 proposal: 8MB blocks, Tachyon shielded pool, quantum-resistant options (Medium confidence). Developer ValarDragon proposed NU8 for a late January 2027 window, including a Tachyon pool designed against future quantum decryption and a fourfold block size rise. It is still in technical review, core engineer str4d has raised objections, and it would need a community vote. KuCoin (TechFlow)

Information only, not advice.

item.title: Tue 10 Nov 19:45 · risk-off · Hot US inflation puts a bigger Fed rate rise on the table
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. US inflation came in hot: prices rose 0.4% in October and core prices 0.3%, both above forecasts.
  2. A Fed rate rise on 9 December now looks certain, and Governor Waller had said core at 0.3% or more would put a half-point rise on the table.
  3. Bitcoin dipped to about $73,400, its weakest since 21 August, then got back above $74,000. US shares gave back part of Monday's rally.

What changed: This morning the open question was whether inflation would cool. It did not, so the debate has moved from whether the Fed hikes in December to by how much. Next to watch: Whether bitcoin's daily close (midnight UTC, midnight UK) holds above $73,000, then US PPI on Fri 13 Nov at 13:30 UK.

Hot US inflation puts a bigger Fed rate rise on the table

Prices rose faster than expected in October. Bitcoin touched an 11-week low before steadying, while Wall Street gave back part of Monday's rally.

US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists had forecast, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Tuesday. Core prices, which strip out food and energy, rose 0.3% against forecasts of 0.2%, CoinDesk reported.

Food rose 0.5% and energy 0.7%, while owners' equivalent rent climbed 0.3%, according to Yahoo Finance. There was again no official annual figure, because last year's government shutdown left a gap in the data.

The report mattered because of what Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said earlier in the day. He backed a quarter-point rise in December even if inflation cooled, and said a half-point move should be considered if core prices rose 0.3% or more, TheStreet reported. Core landed exactly on that line.

Markets moved quickly. The two-year Treasury yield rose 14 basis points to 4.69% and the 10-year reached 4.93%, CoinDesk reported. CME FedWatch put the chance of a half-point move at roughly 15%, with a quarter-point rise the rest.

Bitcoin fell to about $73,400 after the release, its weakest level since 21 August, Bitcoin Magazine and KuCoin reported, before recovering above $74,000. Spot bitcoin funds had already lost $201m on Monday, the seventh straight session of withdrawals from BlackRock's IBIT.

The S&P 500 was down about 0.9% and the Nasdaq 1.3% at midday in New York, according to 24/7 Wall St. Producer prices follow on Friday.

October CPI ran hot (0.4%, core 0.3%), making a December Fed hike look certain and a half-point move possible. Bitcoin touched an 11-week low near $73.4k before steadying above $74k.

  1. 🔴 Outlook changed The Big Picture: US CPI hotter than expected: +0.4% headline, +0.3% core in October (High confidence). Forecasts were +0.3% and +0.2%. Food +0.5%, energy +0.7%, owners' equivalent rent +0.3%. This was the Fed's last CPI before its 8 to 9 December meeting. Still no official annual rate because of the 2025 shutdown gap. CoinDesk Yahoo Finance Bitcoin Magazine
  2. 🔴 New The Big Picture: Waller's half-point trigger was core at 0.3% or more, and core hit 0.3% (High confidence). Fed Governor Waller said before the data that he backs a December hike regardless, and a 50bp move should be considered if core rose 0.3%+. CME FedWatch then showed about 85% for 25bp and 15% for 50bp. The 2-year yield rose 14bp to 4.69%. TheStreet CoinDesk KuCoin News (CME FedWatch) Yahoo Finance
  3. 🔴 Developing Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin dips to about $73.4k, weakest since 21 August, then recovers above $74k (High confidence). It briefly undercut Monday's overnight low of $73,477. Analysts keep naming $73,000 as the level: a daily close below it could open $70,000, while $80,000 is the level to reclaim. Bitcoin Magazine KuCoin News CoinDesk
  4. 🟠 New Markets: Stocks give back part of Monday's rally; 10-year yield nears 5% (High confidence). At midday in New York the S&P 500 was down about 0.9%, the Dow 0.75% and the Nasdaq 1.3%. The 10-year yield reached 4.93%. Higher yields make holding non-yielding assets like bitcoin relatively less attractive. 24/7 Wall St. TheStreet CoinDesk
  5. 🟠 No material change ETFs and Institutions: IBIT's seventh straight day of outflows; Tuesday's figures not yet in (High confidence). Monday's net outflow was $201m across US spot bitcoin ETFs, $213m of it from IBIT. Tuesday's figures normally appear overnight. Bitcoin Magazine Farside Investors
  6. 🟢 No material change Zcash Desk: Zcash: no fresh news since Monday's fall and the 20-second block draft (Medium confidence). ZEC fell 7.9% to about $1,165 on Monday. The NU7.1 proposal to cut block time from 25 to 20 seconds is still a draft awaiting a community vote, with no date. CryptoTicker

item.title: Tue 10 Nov 06:31 · mixed · Bitcoin stuck below $75,000 as Wall Street rallies before inflation test
item.description:
Bitcoin stuck below $75,000 as Wall Street rallies before inflation test

US shares had their best day since April, but bitcoin funds lost another $201m. Today's US price data at 13:30 UK is the next test.

Bitcoin traded at about $74,750 early on Tuesday, CoinDesk reported, having briefly topped $75,000 overnight. On Sunday it fell to roughly $73,500, its lowest level since August, according to Cointelegraph, and about $1.12bn of leveraged positions were liquidated in the 24 hours to Monday morning, per CoinGlass.

Large investors kept selling. US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $201m on Monday, with BlackRock's IBIT losing $213m, according to Farside data. That followed $1.28bn of outflows last week, the largest weekly figure since June, CoinDesk reported, leaving the funds down $914m for the year to date.

Wall Street told a different story. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% on Monday and the Nasdaq 2.74%, led by chipmakers and helped by falling oil prices, even as Nvidia fell 4.3% after its board opened an inquiry into reports that its chief executive was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

Attention now turns to the October consumer price index, due at 13:30 UK time. Economists expect prices to have risen 0.3% on the month, with core inflation at 0.2%, CoinDesk reported. There will be no annual figure because of gaps left by last year's government shutdown. CME FedWatch put the odds of a Federal Reserve rate rise in December at about 79%, Cointelegraph reported.

Analysts cited by CoinDesk named $73,000 as the key support level, with $80,000 the line to reclaim.

Zcash fell 7.9% on Monday to about $1,165, CryptoTicker reported, as a developer proposed cutting block times again to 20 seconds.

Stocks bounced hard on Monday but bitcoin stayed stuck near $74.7k as ETF outflows continued. Today's US inflation print at 13:30 UK decides the next move, with a December Fed hike priced at about 79%.

  1. 🔴 The Big Picture: US CPI today at 13:30 UK; markets price about 79% odds of a Fed hike on 9 Dec (High confidence). Consensus is +0.3% m/m headline and +0.2% core (September: +0.6% and +0.3%). No official year-on-year rate this month because of the 2025 shutdown gap. A hot print would firm up hike bets; a soft core reading could spark a relief bounce. CoinDesk Cointelegraph (CME FedWatch) CryptoTicker
  2. 🔴 Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin about $74.7k after Sunday low near $73.5k, lowest since August (High confidence). About $1.12bn of leveraged positions liquidated in 24h (CoinGlass). Price is below the 50-week average (~$75.5k) and the short-term holder cost basis (~$75.7k). Analysts flag $73k as key support, $68k to $70k below, and $80k as the level to reclaim. CoinDesk Cointelegraph
  3. 🔴 Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin ETFs lose another $201m on Monday after $1.28bn last week (High confidence). IBIT alone saw -$213m. Last week's outflow was the biggest since June and leaves 2026 flows at -$914m, versus $20bn+ inflows in each of the past two years. ETF demand has been the main bid, so the selling caps rallies. Farside Investors KuCoin News (Farside data) CoinDesk Daybook (SoSoValue)
  4. 🟠 Markets: Wall Street's best day since April: S&P +2.35%, Nasdaq +2.74%, Dow +1,104 (High confidence). Chipmakers and falling oil (US crude near $87 to $90) led the rebound. Nvidia fell 4.3% after its board opened an inquiry into reports its CEO was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Bitcoin did not join the rally, a sign crypto-specific selling dominates. US 10-year yield about 4.88%. The Motley Fool StockTitan Cointelegraph
  5. 🟠 Zcash Desk: Zcash falls 7.9% to about $1,165 as dev proposes 20-second blocks (Medium confidence). ZEC has given back its NU7 gains (down 5.1% on the week). A draft proposal for NU7.1 would cut block time from 25s to 20s while keeping daily issuance and the halving date unchanged; it still needs a community vote and has no date. Grayscale's Zcash fund saw $11m out on 5 Nov. CryptoTicker CryptoTicker
  6. 🟢 The Big Picture: China extends US trade truce by two months; Xi and Trump due to meet at APEC next week (Medium confidence). The truce was due to expire today, so the extension removes one near-term shock. Trump also said new strikes on Iran were 'highly unlikely'. CoinDesk Daybook

item.title: Mon 9 Nov 18:00 · risk-off · Bitcoin sags towards $74,000 as Wall Street braces for inflation test
item.description:
Bitcoin sags towards $74,000 as Wall Street braces for inflation test

ETF investors pulled $1.3bn last week. Tomorrow's US price data could decide whether the Fed raises rates in December.

Bitcoin spent Monday close to its lowest level of the week, trading around $74,500 after dipping to roughly $73,700 on Sunday. That is about 8% below the $81,000 high it touched only last Wednesday, according to market data compiled by KuCoin and CryptoTicker.

The slide has come as large investors step back. US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded net outflows of about $1.28bn between 2 and 6 November, with BlackRock's IBIT alone accounting for some $1.21bn, several outlets reported. Over the past 24 hours, roughly $1bn of leveraged positions were forced closed, most of them bets on higher prices.

The wider backdrop is no kinder. The Nasdaq ended last week about 12% below its October record after an AI-led sell-off following the US midterm elections, and futures markets now put the chance of a Federal Reserve rate rise on 9 December at around 80%, Yahoo Finance reported, citing CME FedWatch.

That puts tomorrow's US consumer price index, due at 13:30 UK time, at the centre of the week. Economists expect prices to have risen 0.3% in October, after 0.6% in September. Closer to home, the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% last Thursday.

Zcash, meanwhile, has been steady at about $1,260 since its NU7 upgrade went live on 5 November, cutting block times to 25 seconds.

Bitcoin is near its weekly low around $74.5k after a week of ETF outflows. Tomorrow's US inflation print (13:30 UK) is the big test, with markets pricing a likely Fed hike in December.

  1. 🔴 Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin slips to about $74.5k, weekly low near $73.7k (Medium confidence). Down from an $81k high on 4 Nov. About $1bn of positions were liquidated in 24h, mostly longs. Daily RSI near 35, close to oversold. Support cited at $71.3k to $67.9k, resistance near $75.6k and $78.2k. KuCoin News (CoinGlass data) CryptoTicker weekly recap
  2. 🔴 Bitcoin Desk: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.28bn last week (2 to 6 Nov) (High confidence). BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about $1.21bn. ETF buying has been a main source of demand, so steady outflows remove a key bid. 24/7 Wall St. FinanceFeeds CryptoTicker
  3. 🔴 The Big Picture: US CPI tomorrow 13:30 UK; markets price about 77 to 80% odds of a Fed hike on 9 Dec (High confidence). Consensus is +0.3% m/m headline and +0.2% core (September was +0.6% and +0.3%). No year-on-year figure this month because of the 2025 shutdown data gap. A hot print would firm up hike odds, which has been weighing on bitcoin. FinancialJuice CPI preview Yahoo Finance (CME FedWatch)
  4. 🟠 The Big Picture: Nasdaq in correction, about 12% below its October record after the post-midterm AI sell-off (Medium confidence). Bitcoin has traded with tech in risk-off spells. VIX closed Friday near 25.5: below 20 would signal calm, above 30 real stress. Oil fell to about $98. Yahoo Finance
  5. 🟠 UK: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% (8 to 1, Mann wanted 0.5%) (Medium confidence). Bailey said it is not necessarily the start of a series, but another rise 'could be fairly strong' if the US–Iran conflict drags on. UK inflation seen near 5% by mid-2027. GBP/USD about 1.347: a stronger pound shrinks the £ value of US$-priced BTC, which matters for UK CGT sums. investingLive

About 12,224 ZEC left in the Sprout pool is now unspendable. ZEC about $1,260, roughly flat on the week (+0.8% 7d). The Block CryptoTicker
  7. 🟢 Policy: Democrats won both chambers on 3 Nov; the CLARITY Act lapses on 3 Jan unless the Senate passes it (Medium confidence). The US crypto market-structure bill now needs a lame-duck vote. If it lapses, US rules stay unclear for longer, which keeps a regulatory overhang on US-listed crypto. CryptoTicker Yahoo Finance
